_method: Pad-button convention calibrated from the standard PSX SIO pad bitfield (bit0=Select,3=Start,4=Up,5=Right,6=Down,7=Left,8=L2,9=R2,10=L1,11=R1,12=Triangle,13=Circle,14=Cross,15=Square) and confirmed in-context: bit4/bit6 (Up/Down) drive a stored cursor-index field that a sound plays on CHANGE (cursor_move); bit13 (Circle) drives menu-confirm/purchase/proceed call chains; bit14 (Cross) drives menu-cancel/close call chains. All bit values below are the literal `li $a1,N` immediate passed to the per-button pad-test function at [$s1+0x408] (helper also seen at +0x3f4/+0x3fc for press/hold variants).

evidence.note: Title-screen 'Press Start' blink state machine: counter at [$s1+0x54] increments every frame; at 0x00002a6c `slti $v0,0x258` gates a ~600-frame cycle, sub-counters at +0x56/+0x59 track blink sub-phases; when the sub-phase counter wraps (0x00002ab0 `sltiu $v0,0x3`), code resets fields and at 0x00002afc/0x00002b04 `lw $v0,0x5c48($v0)` / `jalr $v0` with `ori $a0,0x113e` plays SWITCH03 unconditionally -- a periodic logo/title animation beat, not a pad-gated UI action.

SWITCH03.note: Only 1 call site in the whole 470-site sweep (pro/stdwtitl.s), and it fires off a frame counter, not a pad-button branch -- cannot be classified as cursor/confirm/cancel; recorded honestly as an unrelated periodic cue rather than force-fit into the UI-action set.

evidence.note: `li $a1,0xd` (bit 13 = Circle) -> jalr [$s1+0x408] (newly-pressed test) -> `srav $s0,$s0,$v0` / `andi $s0,0x1` -> `beqz $s0,.L0x00001a74` (skip if not pressed) -> `lw $v0,0x5c48($v0)` / `jalr $v0` with `ori $a0,0x503c` plays SYSTEM00, then stores an exit/result code to [$s2+0x14] and jumps to the shared menu-return routine at 0x80084a78 -- fires exactly on Circle-press that closes/commits the current status-menu screen.

Same shape: `li $a1,0xd` (bit 13) at 0x00001314 -> pressed test -> `ori $a0,0x503c` plays SYSTEM00 at 0x00001344, then immediately calls the item's callback at `[a0+0x6f0]` (the 'buy/select this item' function pointer) -- Circle-confirm on the shop item list.

Title screen: `li $a1,0x3` (bit 3 = Start) at 0x00002a00 -> pressed test -> plays SYSTEM00 (`ori $a0,0x503c`) at 0x00002a48 then proceeds into the game-start transition -- same id used for the Start-button 'confirm/proceed' action on a screen with no cursor to move.

`li $a1,0xe` (bit 14 = Cross) at 0x00001a88 -> pressed test -> `beqz $s0,.L0x00001dc8` (skip if not pressed) -> plays SYSTEM01 (`ori $a0,0x50bd`) at 0x00001ab8, then calls `[a0+0x2c]` with `li $a1,0x32` and jumps to the same shared return routine (0x80084a78) used by the SYSTEM00 confirm path -- Cross-cancel sibling of the Circle-confirm branch above.

`li $a1,0xe` (bit 14) at 0x0000146c -> pressed test -> plays SYSTEM01 (`ori $a0,0x50bd`) at 0x0000149c, then calls the item's `[a0+0x6ec]` callback -- a DIFFERENT function pointer than SYSTEM00's `[a0+0x6f0]` 'select' callback in the same struct, i.e. the dedicated cancel/back handler.

`li $a1,0xe` (bit 14) at 0x00003fac -> pressed test -> plays SYSTEM01 (`ori $a0,0x50bd`) at 0x00003fdc, sets a result code (`li $v0,0xc8`) and jumps to the shared exit routine at 0x80086e20 -- third independent overlay agreeing on Cross==SYSTEM01==cancel.

Up (bit 4) and Down (bit 6) newly-pressed tests (0x000018c4/0x0000193c, each paired with a +0x3fc 'held' re-test) update a stored selection index at [$s2+0x70]; at 0x000019a4 `beq $s4,$v0,.L0x000019e8` skips the sound if the index is UNCHANGED from the value cached in $s4 before the frame's input; only when it changed does the code fall through to 0x000019b8 and play SYSTEM02 (`ori $a0,0x513e`) -- classic 'index changed this frame' cursor-move gate.

Identical shape in the shop's item list: Up/Down (bit4/bit6, 0x00001bc8/0x00001c08) update [$s2+0x74]; `beq $s4,$v0,.L0x00001c7c` at 0x00001c38 skips the play call unless the index changed; SYSTEM02 (`ori $a0,0x513e`) plays at 0x00001c4c only on the changed path.

The dialogue-window constructor: allocates the window struct via `jal F0x80014504`, stores the caller-supplied style, and unconditionally plays SYSTEM03 (`lw $v0,%lo(D0x80055c48)($v0)` / `jalr $v0` with `ori $a0,0x19`) as its very last action before returning -- fires exactly once per window creation.

Generic open/close sub-panel helper: `beqz $a1,.L0x000170f8` branches on a boolean opening-direction argument; the TRUE side (falls through) plays SYSTEM03 (`ori $a0,0x19`) at 0x000170d8 before computing a slide-in tween denominator (`li $v0,0x1000; div ...`).

The window's per-frame update function: when the closing-condition callback at `[a0+0x168]` returns true, code sets the window's state field to 2 (`li $v0,0x2` / `sw $v0,0x10($v1)` at 0x8001bce0/ce) and, on the very next lines, plays SYSTEM04 (`lw $v0,%lo(D0x80055c48)($v0)` / `jalr $v0` with `ori $a0,0x1a`) at 0x8001bd24 -- fires exactly on the open-to-closing state transition, the complementary event to F0x8001bb88's unconditional open blip.

Same open/close helper as SYSTEM03's ststatus.s evidence: the FALSE side of `beqz $a1,.L0x000170f8` (i.e. the boolean argument was 0, closing direction) falls into 0x000170f8-0x00017108 and plays SYSTEM04 (`ori $a0,0x1a`) instead of SYSTEM03 -- direct boolean-complement sibling in the same function, same struct field pattern the EXE trace above independently confirms.

`andi $v0,$v1,0xff` masks a low byte of a running value; `bne $v0,$a2,.L0x0000a82c` SKIPS the play call unless the masked value EQUALS a parameter $a2 (a target/threshold), in which case it falls through and plays SYSTEM05 (`ori $a0,0x5341`) at 0x0000a820 -- a counter-reaches-target tick, not a pad-input branch.

A frame counter at [$s2+0x80] increments every tick (0x00003ff8/fc); `slti $v0,0x65` at 0x00004000 gates a ~101-frame period; when the counter wraps (reset to 0x64 at 0x0000400c), the code falls through and plays SYSTEM05 (`ori $a0,0x5341`) at 0x00004058 -- same 'periodic counter tick' shape as fieldstg.s, in a completely different menu (partner-select), agreeing this id is a background/ambient cadence blip rather than a cursor/confirm/cancel action.

SYSTEM05.note: Two independent overlays agree on the SHAPE (counter-driven, not pad-gated) but this doesn't match any of the closed-set UI-action verbs, so it's recorded as other: rather than force-fit to cursor_move/confirm/cancel.

evidence.note: An item-quantity stepper: Up/Down (bit4 at 0x0000b530, bit6 at 0x0000b584) inc/dec a value at [$s2+0x7c], clamped to a max derived from [$s2+0x5c]; `beq $s3,$v0,.L0x0000b630` at 0x0000b60c skips the sound unless the stepped value differs from the cached $s3; SYSTEM06 (`ori $a0,0x1b`) plays at 0x0000b620 only on the changed path -- same 'value changed' gate as SYSTEM02, in a numeric-stepper context instead of a list cursor.

The shop's buy-quantity stepper: value at [$s2+0x78] is incremented/decremented (clamped against the item's stock count via a callback at 0xb44c), `beq $s4,$a0,.L0x00002720` at 0x000026c4 skips the play call unless changed, and SYSTEM06 (`ori $a0,0x1b`) plays at 0x00002708 on the changed path -- confirms the same id/action in a second, independent overlay.

Continuing the quantity-stepper function above: Circle (bit 13) tested at 0x0000b64c -> pressed -> plays SYSTEM07 (`ori $a0,0x1c`) at 0x0000b67c, then clears the stepper's active-flag fields ([$s2+0x78]/[$s2+0x74]), sets a result code (`li $v0,0x1`) and jumps to the shared exit routine (0x8008e728) -- Circle-confirm that commits the stepped value, mirroring SYSTEM00's role but scoped to this stepper widget.

The shop's buy-quantity stepper: Circle (bit 13) tested at 0x0000273c -> pressed -> plays SYSTEM07 (`ori $a0,0x1c`) at 0x0000276c, then immediately runs the purchase-commit call chain (price lookup, stock-count callback, then the buy-confirm dialog at `[a0+0x244]`) -- Circle-confirm gate on the quantity, confirmed in a second overlay.

_SYSTEM08_note: SYSTEM08 (id 0x800454c4) has zero entries in soundtst-common-call-sites.json's 470 sites -- no disassembled call site to trace, so it is intentionally omitted from this table rather than guessed.
